notes: The 7 points on p2.answer-passages sit right on the line between 7 and 4, and 2 of the 4 passing pages are borderline calls. p7's real lead paragraph is 282 Chinese characters, above the 50–200 ceiling; it passes on the strength of several 50–63 character prose passages at 29%–62% depth (the shortest of them is exactly 50 characters, right on the line). p8's lead is 204 characters, over by 4. If "the front of the body" is read strictly as the first 20% of the body, p7 fails, this check drops to 4 points (present on a few pages), and the total becomes 66 — still in the Solid band, but with 0 points of headroom. If the 200-character ceiling is read as a reference rather than a hard boundary, p7 and p8 pass on their leads alone and the result is unchanged. That is, these 7 points are fragile downward and firm upward.

Whether p2.freshness gets 3 or 0 is the most contestable call in this audit. The only reader-visible dates across the 8 sampled pages are p7's 「2021年5月 启用日期」 and p8's 「2026年3月 启用日期」 — these are the go-live dates of the customers' systems, not the pages' publication or update dates. None of the 8 pages has datePublished, dateModified or article:published_time, and none carries an "updated on" line. I scored 3 under v1.1's rule that a freshness signal is about whether readers and crawlers can establish currency, because for a case study the go-live date does let a reader judge how old it is; but classing it as content data and scoring 0 is equally defensible, and that would put the total at 66, exactly on a band boundary. Two further items I deliberately left out: the footer 「© 2012- 2026」 is by convention not a freshness signal; and the sitemap's 296/296 lastmod and the HTTP Last-Modified header on the data-model pages were not counted either, because the tier wording is limited to "the page and its structured data" — though the latter is in fact a usable freshness signal for a crawler, which is something the rubric itself could reconsider.

The 2 points on p3.video reflect a rubric that runs out of tiers, not a difficult judgement. 471 videos on Bilibili, 13643 followers and 16 collections are the opposite of tier 2's description of "sporadic content"; but tier 3 binds "sustained output" together with "VideoObject on the site", and VideoObject gets 0 hits site-wide, so the score is capped at 2. The result understates the channel and overstates the markup at the same time. Recommend that v1.2 split these two conditions; otherwise every Chinese site with plenty of content and no schema lands in the same box.

The 0 on p3.knowledge-graph carries residual uncertainty. Wikidata and Chinese Wikipedia I confirmed empty by API (wbsearchentities returned search:[] for all three of 明道云, 上海万企明道软件 and 明道云HAP), but Baidu Baike returned 403 「百度安全验证」 to every user-agent I tried — neither a direct request nor WebFetch got through — so the judgement rests indirectly on two rounds of site-restricted search. Those searches brought back an entry for the founder 任向晖 and one for the predecessor product 「明道（梅花信息推出的企业软件平台）」, plus entries for the competitors 简道云 and 得帆, but nothing for 明道云 itself. For a Chinese SaaS, Baidu Baike is exactly the place most likely to hold an entry, and it is exactly the one I could not verify. If a 明道云 entry does exist, this check should be 4 points, the total 73, and the band unchanged.

Sampling luck magnifies the error on p1.breadcrumb and p1.page-type. Only one page family on the whole site — /landing/data-model/, 153 pages — carries BreadcrumbList + TechArticle + ItemList, and my 8 URLs happened to catch exactly 1 page of it. One more page from that family and breadcrumb could have reached "generally present on hierarchical pages"; one fewer and both checks would be 0. The 8-page sample is the rubric's rule, but for a site where one page family is done well and four have nothing, it is a high-variance instrument. The more honest statement: the structured data on the data-model family is fairly complete, and the hap/, compare/, solution/ and case/ families are essentially bare — that fact is more useful than whether the score is 2 or 3.

The 3 points on p4.question-coverage hinge on one definition question. I counted only "a dedicated page answers it head on", so both 「什么是零代码、和低代码有什么区别」 (/zerocode, /whatiszerocode and /faq all 404; no terminology page among the 296 sitemap entries) and 「安全合规与信创」 (/security and /trust both 404; only a section inside /hap/feature) count as uncovered, giving 8/10. Counting that security section as coverage would make it 9/10 and this check 4 points. I also limited coverage to www.mingdao.com: blog.mingdao.com updates several times a week (the top three entries are dated 2026-09-02, 2026-09-01 and 2026-08-27, all with visible dates) and would most likely supply the zero-code definition — but it is a different host, it is not in www's sitemap, and more to the point it is not in llms.txt either (llms.txt lists apidoc but not blog or help). The freshest and most content-like part of the site is precisely the part nothing points to.

The 5 points on p1.organization rest on 7 of 8 pages, with one inconsistency worth naming: the data-model page's Organization node has only name+url and the page has no WebSite node at all — "both present, including logo" holds for the Next.js www template but not for the static /landing/ page family. And the logo that template declares (fp1.mingdaoyun.cn/open/img/logo.png) tests as 403, 304 bytes, returning HTML rather than PNG. Fix that link and add sameAs — the footer already carries five accounts (Bilibili, WeChat official account, WeChat Channels, Douyin, Xiaohongshu), they just never reach the schema — and the sixth point is there for the taking.

The v1.1 calibration file back-projects mingdao.com at 50% (Getting Started); I measured 69%. I did not re-check the item-by-item evidence from the v1.0 run, but what I saw this time — a robots.txt naming 15 retrieval user-agents and carrying Content-Signal, a 5695-byte llms.txt with 48 of 49 links reachable, working Accept: text/markdown content negotiation, .well-known/mcp.json and an agent-skills index — does not look like the site that projection was based on. The 19-point gap should be read as "the site changed", not as "the rubric drifted", and my 69 certainly cannot be used to argue backwards for the accuracy of the projection method. It also bears out what the calibration file itself states: no real audit re-run under v1.1 had been performed before this.

citation.note: Not measured, not scored. Under v1.1, AI citation performance is an outcome metric: it requires putting real industry questions to ChatGPT / Perplexity / Doubao / Ernie and other engines one by one and observing whether the site is cited. The same question asked repeatedly yields different results, so it is not reproducible, and it is determined jointly by readiness and by time. This audit covers only the readiness part — externally observable and fixable by the site owner. Citation performance should be reported as a separate block in its own right and not folded into the 69 points above.
